[Javaagent] Method name / annotation mismatch: this method is annotated `@Advice.OnMethodExit` but named `onEnter`. Looks like a copy-paste from the other advices; rename to `onExit` to match the annotation (the repo style explicitly flags this as a copy-paste bug pattern).

```suggestion
    public static PartialFunction<Throwable, BoxedUnit> onExit(
```

[Javaagent] This `throw` is inside a netty `ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter.channelRead(...)` that we install ourselves into the user's pipeline. Unlike the throws inside advice methods, this is not wrapped by ByteBuddy `suppress = Throwable.class` — it propagates straight back through netty and into the application. Per the javaagent rule "never throw exceptions in javaagent code", drop the throw (the comments above already note this branch shouldn't be reachable). Either log at FINE and continue, or just fall through to `super.channelRead(ctx, msg)`.

[Javaagent] Same pattern: a helper called from advice should not throw. The advice that calls this method has `suppress = Throwable.class`, so the IAE is swallowed at runtime, but it still corrupts the request flow silently for any future caller that doesn't suppress. The comment above already says "shouldn't practically reach here" — prefer returning without setting the context (and optionally logging at FINE) instead of throwing.

[Javaagent] `ApplyAdvice` will NPE if `PROMISE_K_CONTEXT_FIELD.get(thiz)` returns `null` (e.g. because `Promise$Transformer` was constructed via a constructor not matched by `TrapContextAdvice`, or the virtual field is not set yet during early class loading). The throw is suppressed by `suppress = Throwable.class`, but it disables instrumentation on that promise and produces noise. Two small fixes:
- mark `onApplyEnter`'s return and the `@Advice.Enter Scope` parameter on `onApplyExit` as `@Nullable`, return `null` when `savedContext == null`, and null-guard `scope.close()` in `onApplyExit`.
- this also matches the pattern already used in `GenStreamingServerDispatcherInstrumentation.DispatchAdvice`.

[Javaagent] `methodEnter` can return `null` (the `req instanceof Request` branch is taken or `request.ctx().apply(...)` returns `null` when the bridging instrumentation hasn't run for this request). The exit advice already handles a `null` `Scope`, so just add `@Nullable` (and the corresponding import) on the return type here and on the `@Advice.Enter Scope scope` parameter in `methodExit` for accuracy and consistency with the rest of this PR. Also worth null-guarding `context.makeCurrent()` defensively (`return context == null ? null : context.makeCurrent();`) — the comment says it shouldn't be null, but if it ever is, the suppressed NPE silently breaks request propagation.

[Style] `OTEL_NETTY_HANDLER` is only referenced inside this class (used as the handler name in `mutateHandlerPipeline`). Prefer `private` over `public` for visibility — minimal-necessary-visibility per the style guide.

```suggestion
  private static final String OTEL_NETTY_HANDLER = "otelFinagleNettyHandler";
```

check out the `compile-stub` pattern for cases like this — see [writing-instrumentation.md](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/docs/contributing/writing-instrumentation.md#instrumenting-code-that-is-not-available-as-a-maven-dependency) (the doc focuses on missing Maven artifacts, but the same mechanism should handle inaccessible/package-private types like `Promise.K`). Existing examples: [`liberty/compile-stub`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/tree/main/instrumentation/liberty/compile-stub), [`internal-class-loader/compile-stub`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/tree/main/instrumentation/internal/internal-class-loader/compile-stub).

Suggested:

- Move `Promise.java` into a new sibling module `instrumentation/finagle-http-23.11/compile-stub/` at `src/main/java/com/twitter/util/Promise.java`.
- In `javaagent/build.gradle.kts`, replace the `tasks.withType<Jar>().configureEach { exclude(...) }` block with:
  ```kotlin
  compileOnly(project(":instrumentation:finagle-http-23.11:compile-stub"))

[Javaagent] Per the advice-patterns convention, advice references in `transform()` should use `getClass().getName() + "$InnerAdvice"` rather than a `.class` literal — the class literal triggers unwanted class loading in `transform()`.

```suggestion
        isConstructor(), getClass().getName() + "$ConstructorAdvice");
```

```

```

[General] Comment is incorrect/misleading. The stub module is consumed via `compileOnly(project(":instrumentation:finagle-http-23.11:compile-stub"))` in the javaagent build, so these classes are never on the runtime classpath and never end up in the agent jar — there is no "strip at jar construction" step in `build.gradle.kts`. Suggest rewording to reflect the actual mechanism (compile-only dependency).
